text.p: SmartServer for KNX is a product which allows to remote clients (to visualization programs) to read and write data from KNX bus. SmartServer is designed for continuous running, it is present in the operating system as a service. SmartServer KNX keeps data in the cache, so their current values are available for clients continually. Server can be remotely administrated by web interface (HTTP/HTML).
Server provides for clients two interfaces: XMLSocket and line-oriented text TCP/IP interface.

Before all, SmartServer's aim is to communicate data of KNX bus. Pure KNX is not fully capable to realize some functions easily, so SmartServer is supplied with functional modules to support missing KNX functionality as well. Modules can directly access all SmartServer's data, they can be linked to visualization (e.g. using HTTP), what together allows customizing the control system exactly by user's needs.

Functional modules in SmartServer determine structure of its dataeither KNX data, or data of functional modules, or SmartServer system data have to be accessible by clients (if needed all simultaneously). Current SmartServer version does not support changing data inside functional modules, but data model is already prepared to do so.

SmartServer data is identified by name (identifier), which is hierarchical and can be compound. Parts of the name corresponding to hierarchy level are divided with dot (. character). As the name can be long, usually some method of its shortening is available.

Contexts can be switched in the places where it is meaningful. Switching can simplify configuration or client application, because it allows using shorter names. Switching (or setting) of context is described further in the particular chapters.

The SmartServer runs as a service of operation system and it starts immediately after installation. It loads all its settings (KNX objects, communication, KNXnet/IPinterface) from a text file on the disc (description, see bellow), which is allotted to the server with help of administrative web interface. The configuration file cannot be modified with help of the administrative interface, the file must be recorded on the disc by another way (locally, with help of RDP, VNC, TeamViewer, etc.).

default.cfg configuration file is located in the same folder, as the server program (KNXSrv.exe). It is installed by the installer and it contains all available parameters with brief comments. Settings are usually switched off by default (using commentaries).

Program running as the service has limited possibilities of interaction with user, therefore it is not possible to find out its proper loading from configuration file directly. Error messages about configuration are available in administrative interface only. The configuration can be checked also before its setting with help of tool of checkcfg.exe command line, which is delivered as a part of server installation.

Configuration files for server are text ones, structured to sections ones (section names are between [ a ] characters) and line oriented ones (parameters are recorded inside sections on independent lines).
Sample configuration files are stored in Examples folder with the server program.

text.p: [objects] and [blocks] sections summarize all definitions of KNX data items, which should be known to server and with which the server should communicate. [read_start] contains parameters for control of initial loading, i.e. of the first loading of tracker_init and transmitter_with_status_init objects after start of the server (see the chapter ). The server loads such selected data objects in block procedurally and tries to load them all. To prevent an overloading of the data bus at starting (e.g., to allow recording to KNX just from the starting), the server puts delays between loadings of single data objects (delay parameter). If some of objects cannot be loaded, the server tries, after lapse of recovery delay ([interface] read_on_start_delay, the chapter ), to obtain them repeatedly by new loading. The server proceeds by this way, till it will not exhaust the permitted number of initial loadings (parameter [interface] read_on_start_repeat_count, see the chapter ).
If no problems occur in communication at starting, there is recommended to leave the initial values of parameters (e.g., not to enter read_start section to the configuration file).

E.g., at loading of 100 data objects the obtaining of the value itself (without repetition and recovery) lasts in total 15 seconds (150ms100). Of course, during this time it is possible to load to the data bus arbitrarily, nevertheless, the data for clients need not be valid yet (in such case the server will return zero, false or empty text to clients).

section.title: Import of data items from ETS

text.p: The definition of data items of the server may be significantly accelerated in cooperation with ETS program. ETS can (according to its configuration) export group addresses of the project to the text file determined for OPC server (KNX Association product, as well as ETS). This file (with ESF extension) can accept the server configuration and use all data items from it. ESF file need not contain always all necessary information, nevertheless, the server can deal with missing data (according to the setting, see below).
The server will accept the data objects from ESF file inside [objects] section with help of esf_adapt, esf_strict and esf_ignore parameters with the meaning according to table .

tr.td: Data items without accurate data type will be accepted, their type will be modified according to typical use and the configuration will be loaded.
Data items without accurate data type will be refused and the configuration will not be loaded (errors will be reported).
Data items without accurate data type will be ignored and the configuration will be loaded (the server will not know the data ones, without types of items).

text.p: All types recorded as EIS1EIS15 are considered for accurate data types. Inaccurate data types are shown in ESF file in the form, e.g. Uncertain (3 byte), which allows (as mentioned above), at use of esf_adapt parameter, to select a suitable type automatically. If this is not successful, then the loading of configuration will finish with error message.
At loading of esf_adapt configuration, the server will convert inaccurate types to accurate ones according to table .

text.p: An example of the server configuration with help of ESF is stored in 09 ETS-Opc.cfg and 09 test.esf files.

At its run, the server can record information about current status and running operations. It can be useful, e.g., at solution of problems with communications. On the start, the listings are not switched-on, [log], [datalog], [httplog] and [networklog] configuration file sections serves for their switching-on and setting. Debugging information are not necessary for current operation.

The output of debugging information is the text and the line one, and this it is easily legible. The input setting of the server allows to monitor the listings with help of web interface, after modification of the configurationall data can be stored to the file. Messages of [log] and [networklog] sections have common formát (see below), [httplog] section uses Common Log Format, [datalog] section has special format.
The example of [log] section records:

The date and time of the listing are in the first part, in square brackets. All debugging listings are in UTC time, which is one hour less in comparison with the civil Czech time in winter, and two hours less in summer. Example: A listing with the time 18:06:03.828 was acquired on April 1st, so the corresponding civil time of acquirement is 20:06:03,828.

dl.caption: The second part, an independent letter, codes the kind of the report. The possibilities are as follows (they are classified from the most detail to the most important ones):

dd.p: debugging report, the second level of details
common report, additional information
debugging report, the first level of details
common report, warning against possible troubles at certain situation
debugging report, important information
common report, error of the protocol, status or program, the server is able to continue in operation
debugging report, information about the error
common report, fatal error of the program, the server is not able to continue in operation

dl.caption: The third part of the report distinguishes the origin of the report; reports from following sources appears in the server:

dd.p: Connection with KNX interface, information about KNXnet/IP protocol.
Web server, information about page transfers to clients.
Net server for client connections, information about establishing and termination of connection and about transmission blocks.
SDAP server, information about commands and responses received through SDAP.
XMLSocket server, information about commands and responses received through XMLSocket.

text.p: Behind the third part in the debugging report there follows a text, which is not longer formalised and which contains any data (such ones, which the origin wants to show).

The most frequent reason for use of debugging reports is the communication with help of KNXnet/IP protocol, i.e. the communication with KNX interface. The interface is an independent element outside the server control, which may be switched on or off independently, or which may be used by somebody else for connection with KNX. In every such case, the server has not connection with KNX and it is necessary to switch on the debugging listings for diagnostics of troubles.
The chapter is addressed to diagnostics and debugging listings as well.

The SmartServer supports both kinds of communication with KNX, which are usable for transmission of data. Other kinds, which serve for KNX configuration and programming, are not supported by the SmartServer. The SmartServer is not a tool for programming of elements in KNX data bus.

dl.caption: The kind of communication is governed by mode parameter of [device] section of the configuration file (see ). Following guide-post can be used for selection of the kind of communication:
dl.dt: Does the interface support tunnelling only?

dd.p: This is valid practically for all interfaces available on the market. tunnelling or tunnelling-NAT must be used.
Its name will probably contain router, or it will be some sort of PLC. Any kind of communication can be usedtunnelling, tunnelling-NAT or routing.
Nevertheless, because the router is determined just for transmission of data communication from KNX to IP network and back, it is recommended to select the kind of routing.

dl.dt: Does the server or interface occur behind the router?

dd.p: The only variant will be tunnelling-NAT probably.

dl.dt: Is the interface produced by other manufacturer than Siemens?

dd.p: There may be problems with tunnelling-NAT connection. Transfer through NAT is Siemens design, which evades KNX standard by this solution. On the other hand, the communication with the interface behaves according to customs in IP networks. In present time, also ETS supports the transfer through NAT, so it can be expected that also another producers than Siemens will support this kind of communication.

Nevertheless, till the tunnelling-NAT will be declared for standard solution, before its use it is necessary to verify (including connection behind NAT), if selected KNX interface does not have problems with it.

text.p: Routers in IP communications are located always between networks and logically connect them. Properly set router transmits all KNX operation between networks without problems, nevertheless, KNXnet/IP character may cause troubles in real cases.

dl.caption: Problem issues for KNXnet/IP may be:

dd.p: Communication by the way of routing runs with help of IP multicasting, when one sent packet can be received by more IP recipients. Used IP multicasting is easily recognizable according to IP addressmulticast addresses start with number 224 and higher (e.g. 225.100.1.5).Switches and routers must be able to recognize and properly send the IP multicasting, which is not always true. At selection of the switch and router for kind of communication of routing it is always necessary to assure knowledge of IP multicasting element.

NAT is a technology allowing exchanging of addresses and ports of senders and recipients in communication. The most frequent use of NAT is currently highly single-purpose onein home and office routersfor connection of smaller network to Internet. To allow transfer between the SmartServer and interface through such KNXnet/IP communication router, it is always necessary to adjust setting of the router (of course, the router must be able to do it).

KNXnet/IP communication is UDP, a permanent connection is not established between elements, therefore the router must know, which data should be forwarded and where. For successful transfer through NAT router there must be assured that the external packet (from Internet, from WAN interface of the router) will direct the router inside to real equipment (to computer with the SmartServer or KNX interface). Routers usually decide about routing according to the protocol type (UDP) and the port number (if port is not changed, then number 3671 is valid for KNXnet/IP). In their configuration then there will exist a rule (port forwarding, for triggering, server inside, etc.), which will perform the UDP communication on selected port of the equipment with internal IP address. An accurate configuration differs router from router, nevertheless, the router configuration can be managed by any network specialist.
The transfer of data packages with help of NAT from inside of the network out (to Internet) usually need not be configured by any way.

To allow the operation of KNXnet/IP communication between the SmartServer a the KNX interface, all NAT routers on the route must be set properly. Typical case is, e.g., an interconnection of two smaller networks through Internet, when both networks have NAT routers on their interfaces. Both these routers must have configured transfer of external KNXnet/IP packages to internal network.

dl.dt: Computer with more network cards, routers

dd.p: The tunnel communication in KNXnet/IP requires the client to announce to the server (KNX interface) its IP address (SmartServer) inside the data packet. The server will consequently send the response to this IP address. If a computer has more network cards (two Ethernet interface, Ethernet+WiFi, etc.), or if data pass through the router to another networks, then the communication by the way of tunnelling need not be successful.

In the first case (more network cards), an interface may get an address of improper interface in the data package, so its response may be sent on improper route and it will not reach the client (SmartServer).

In the second case (transfer through router), a local address may be stored to the data package in target network (where KNX interface has no sense, or is duplicated one, respectively). In such case, the interface either is not able to send the response at all, or will send it to another equipment.
If the above-mentioned troubles occur, it is recommended to use tunnelling-NAT or routing kind of communication.

text.p: If the connection is configured and despite of it, the server cannot be connected, the simplest way is to use the diagnostic listings (see chapter ). Debugging listings will provide information, based on which it is possible to determine the reason of troubles easier.

Listings connected with KNX interface originate from KNX/KNXnet.Connection source and they cover establishing and disconnection of connection, data transfer (in all modes) and control information. Listings with word CONNECT and LISTENING relate to establishing of connection, listings with word DISCONNECT relate to disconnection of the connection. Data transferred by tunnel connection contain words SEND or RECEIVE, data transferred with help of routing contain words ROUTED IN or ROUTED OUT.

During its duration, each connection with KNX interface is designated by number. An interface assigns the number of connection, usually each new connection gets the number higher by one. The number is important for diagnostics of communication with KNX, because it must stay unchanged during one connection. If the number of connection is changed in debugging listings, then something is probably wrong in the communication. Following example shows listings of connection (only some lines are selected from the record) with number 99:
text.p.type: [3.450] t KNX/KNXnet.Connection: CONNECTed in TUNNELING mode: 99 10.0.0.6:3671 [3.700] t KNX/KNXnet.Connection: RECEIVE 99 group: 2/1/30 [3.970] t KNX/KNXnet.Connection: SEND 99 group: 2/1/30 true [4.241] t KNX/KNXnet.Connection: DISCONNECT request: 99 10.0.0.6:3671 [4.251] t KNX/KNXnet.Connection: DISCONNECTed: 99 10.0.0.6:3671

text.p.type: [0.644] t KNX/KNXnet.Connection: CONNECT request: 10.0.0.16:3671 [0.661] t KNX/KNXnet.Connection: CONNECT timeout ... [9.130] t KNX/KNXnet.Connection: CONNECT request: 10.0.0.6:3671 [9.140] t KNX/KNXnet.Connection: CONNECT failure: 36 10.0.0.6:3671 [9.140] t KNX/KNXnet.Connection: DISCONNECTed: 0 10.0.0.6:3671
text.p: In the first case, the server was not connected with KNX interface, because no response came in the frame of determined time (timeout). The most frequent reasons of this behaviour are: IP address or port addresses of the interface wrongly introduced, interface disconnected from network and network unavailability of interface (e.g. if the interface is behind NAT interface, etc.).

dl.caption: In the second unsuccessful case the server interface found the connection, but the interface refused the connection with error 36. Error codes are the part of KNX standard (KNX Std 3.8.1), which currently defines following errors:

dd.p: Interface does not support requested kind of connection. E.g., the server requests the tunnel connection, but the interface does not know it.
Interface does not support requested setting of connection. Presently not used.
Interface does not allow the connection, because its maximum number of connections is already exhausted.

This error is the most frequent one, because current KNX interface allows only one tunnel connection. If something else (other server, ETS) is connected to the interface, then connection of the server is not successful. The error may be caused also by outages of power-supply or network: if the server will not terminate the connection (e.g. at forced switch-off of the computer), then the interface waits for two minutes, before it allow to establish a new connection.

dl.caption: A simple procedure for finding out of problems with connection may be, e.g., as follows:
dl.dt: Attempt for connection finishes with error timeout

dd.p: Check the network cable (ping on interface address must be successful), check if the interface is powered on.

Verify, if interface is running (if it is supplied, etc.). Make sure that you use the proper address and the interface port. If the interface is in local network, then with help of discover tool (part of server installation) find out addresses and ports of available interfaces.

If the interface is in a foreign network (if you are connected through Internet), then verify, if the UDP transfer in both directions (outside and inside) of selected port is allowed on routers between the server and the interface. Verify, if you are using the tunnelling-ACK kind of connection in such case.
If you are using the routing kind of connection, then verify, if routers and switches between the server and the interface support and properly work with IP multicast packets.

dl.dt: Attempt for connection finishes with error failure: XX

dd.p: If you are using the tunnelling or tunnelling-ACK kinds of connection, then verify, if another server, ETS, or some other program is not connected to the interface. In an affirmative case, disconnect it.

Make sure that during last two minutes an outage of server did not occur (forced switching-off of the computer, forced stopping of the server process). In affirmative case, wait two minutes or switch off and switch on the interface power supply.

section.title: Location of source data and access

text.p: For administration and for user’s web pages connected with data from KNX, the SmartServer provides an embedded web server. Administrative part is protected by name and password, user’s web pages are free available. The server runs on IP port 6005 (the port can be changed in configuration, see the chapter).

Administrative part of the server is available on the address http://[server]:6005/SmartServer, user’s part of the server is available on the address http://[server]:6005/SmartServer/User ([server] must be replaced with the name or address of the computer, for a local computer there will be valid, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:6005/SmartServer). All files, which should be available with help of server, must be stored in User folder (and in subfolders, for details, see ).

Administrative interface is distributed to several pages protected by name and password. After insertion URL http://[server]:6005/SmartServer to the address line of Internet browser and clicking on Private pages link the SmartServer enters to the administrative interface. Following page Login requires input of login data. After the SmartServer installation, the name admin and the password admin is the valid couple.
The login to the administrative interface is timely limited and expires after 30 minutes of inactivity.

dl.caption: The administrative interface consists from following pages:

dd.p: Introductory page with quick survey of status of server and its licence.

The possibility of connection and disconnection of the SmartServer with/from KNX interface is important. E.g., if KNX interface is shared and used currently as for configuration, as for programming of the equipment in KNX, then the SmartServer must be disconnected before ETS connection and connected again after completion of programming (otherwise the SmartServer will not provide valid data to clients).

dl.dd:
Page for setting of the server configuration. It is possible to switch on and to switch off both client interface (SDAP client, XMLSocket client) and it is possible to change the server configuration.
The interface does not allow to load the configuration with help of browser or file and the configuration must enter to computer with the SmartServer by another way (with help of RDP, etc.). The configuration is changed after specification of the route to the configuration file (actual configuration file is filled in advance) and press of Apply push-button. E.g., at modification of setting of connection or at addition of new data objects, the configuration file is modified first (the new one is prepared) and is consequently applied by press of Apply push-button, without necessity to restart the SmartServer service.
With help of Save... linkthe actual configuration file can be loaded and stored in local computer.
Under the line with configuration and push-buttons, there is an area with listing of errors found out at loading of the configuration. If the configuration is OK (e.g. if it was checked in advance with help of checkcfg installed tool), always one line will be added about successful loading of the configuration. Loading of configuration with help of Use push-button replaces only the configuration related to data objects of the server and to communication with KNX. The server accepts the system configuration, i.e. the configuration file section ([log], [datalog] (), [web] () and [users] ()), at its start only.

dd.p: The page displays the history of data operation of the server. In the list arranged from the newest events to the oldest ones there occurs following eventsUPDATE (receipt of data from data bus), SET OK (successful record), SET FAILED (starting of the record failed, e.g., if the SmartServer is not just connected to the data bus) and SET ERROR (the record was started, but finished with error).

Only such data objects occurs in the history, which was created in the configuration with help of logged_objects, logged_objects_on_change, logged_object and logged_object_on_change parameters (see chapter ).

The page with system records will be mostly empty. Especially debugging and diagnostic listings are included among records, which are not listed, if they are not switched on. If the listings are switched on in [log] section, (see ), they will appear just here.
Simple page allowing directly record and load the server data objects. As web interface is interface to whole SmartServer, not only to KNX, all data names must be entered complete, incuding context.

Read value requires insertion of the group address (e.g. .KNX.3/2/3) to the field on the left from Load push-button and its press. The SmartServer will write the value or information about loading error.

Write value works analogously, nevertheless, there is further requested an insertion of recorded value in the second field. E.g., if logic one should be recorded to the bit address 3/1/1, it is set to the field with value true. After press of Write push-button, the SmartServer will announce the result of the record (and on Data history page one can check the feature of the writing).
Page with two areas for editing of roles and users. The page is intended for two main goals: to set up access to administration web interface and to set up access to user defined pages.
Two of roles (sysadmin a sysuser) are system and it is not possible to edit neither delete them. These roles are not listed in role list, but they can be selected for user role.
System users (admin a user by default) read from configuration file (default.cfg, e.g.) also cannot be removed neither edited. Their passwords can be changed arbitrarily.

warning.p: Definition of users can be removed from the configuration file. Then, only users defined using web interface will be available. It is possible, that no user with sysadmin role will exist after the change, and the administration of SmartServer will not possible (there will be no way how to log in).

dl.caption: Editing of roles and users is simple. Web interface offers the following operations:

dd.p: The form with user or role data is opened. After pressing Accept button the role or user will be created, also it is possible to get back (and not to create anything) using link Go back to users list.
Deletes particular role or user.
The same form as for creating user/role is opened. After data modification, changes again can be accepted using Accept button or revoked by using back link.

text.p: All files in Web/User folder of the installation folder may be displayed without a login. E.g., index.html example file (part of the server installation), present in this folder, will be available in local computer as http://127.0.0.1:6005/SmartServer/User/index.html.

Among files (current static HTML, figures, styles), there may be located files with pt.xml extension (e.g. example.pt.xml, which is a part of installation), which the SmartServer processes dynamically and thus allows to input live data of data objects from KNX inside their contents. pt.xml files are XML, therefore they must be well formed and for use in the SmartServer they must have defined XML namespace http://www.smartcontrol.cz/2008/XML/Web/PageTemplate. If it will have proper suffix and wrong namespace, the Smart-Server will not process it as dynamical one and will not input live data to it.
For creation of own user’s pages with live data there is recommended for all cases to create a copy of the example file and modify this copy.

Live data get to the page with help of get function closed to signs ${ a }. The SmartServer searches these signs and replaces them with actual value. Similarly it is possible to record a value to KNX using set function. The record of value requires the user’s activity (press of push-button, reference), therefore the SmartServer in user’s dynamic (pt.xml) pages accepts set function as parameter of reference on page (on another one or on itself). It is also possible to use a selection command (pt:choose) inside dynamic pages, which allows to create the different contents of the page according to different values of logic data objects.

get function is completed with similar function getwix, which is, before all, intended to be used together with Wix visualization tool (see www.papouch.com). getwix function is described further in the chapter .

section.title: Restricting an access to user pages

text.p: SmartServer allows restricting of access to all user pages rendered from pt.xml files. Restricting of access to, e.g., text files or images is not supported.

il.caption: Model of access control mechanism is simple:

li.p: pt.xml file (aka page) determines, which user roles will be allowed to access. Typically each pt.xml file is bound to single role (but they can be many).
Administrator (user with sysadmin role) defines these roles and binds them to users (users must be defined too, usually independently).

When restricted page is accessed SmartServer checks which user is logged in. If user's role is correct, restricted page is immediately displayed. If user's role is not correct, the page with login request is displayed first.
If user with correct role logs in, SmartServer displays requested page.
Administrator (user with sysadmin role) is allowed to access all pages.

il.caption: There are two kind of roles:

li.p: role, which requires full user login (both name and password),
role, which allows login using password (code, usually numerical) only.

text.p: Users are always defined fully, including both name and password. The differentiation, whether the name will be used or not, is a property of the role which takes place just after the role is assigned to particular user.
Role allows logging in using password (key) only, if there is Login by code only check box checked in Role editing form.

warning.p: If more users with key-only login role use the same password, the resulting logged in user is not precisely determined and any of them sharing the same password (key) will be logged in.

Functional modules of SmartServer enhance KNX possibilities. Logical functions, computations or algorithms can be solved using common KNX devices only hardly, functional modules allows realizing some of tasks of the kind. Different SmartServer versions can contain different functional modules.
The configuration of functional modules is described independently in section.

Functional module, which enables SmartServer to store data surviving its power down. For that goal, SmartServer writes data to the file always it changes. On the opposite, when SmartServer starts, data from the file are read out and written into SmartServer.

The file is created on the disk during the first start of SmartServer. SmartServer does not store all data, but only these ones defined in the configuration. It allows differentiate values needed to survive (like configuration data, thermostat base values or so) from values not needed to survive (like current temperatures).

il.caption: Data is defined in the configuration including its initial value, what allows to use module for two purposes:

li.p: If data value does not change in KNXconfigured initial value is written to KNX once during start. During run nothing is stored. Data used this way is constant and can be used for example as configuration parameter.

If data value changes in KNX (e.g. it is mentioned base temperature of thermostat)persisted valued read from the file is written to KNX during start, during run time value is stored to the file if data item is changes. If no value is persisted yet during start, initial configured value is written to KNX.

text.p: Persisting storage module cooperates with initial reading of KNX data (see sekci section). Persisted data can be changed in KNX during SmartServer outage and SmartServer would replace current value with improper (older) one. That is why persisting storage module writes its data just after initial reading finishes.

To make persisting storage really persistent, data file must be located in disk surviving outage. This is common in mainstream operating system, but uncommon in embedded operating systems. For these systems data file must be placed to some external disk (USB, eSATA).

Functional module allowing more outputs to be written after single input change. Because scenes in KNX behave similarly (some value of scene group address makes more devices to set their outputs), the module is named scenes in short. Of course, its possibilities are broader.

li.p: Scenes are logically grouped by inputssingle input controls (using its value) more outputs. In the configuration, the grouping corresponds to sections: main section [scenes] contains list of all inputs together with output sections. These output [scene_<scene_name>] sections of the configuration then contain output values only.

Each output can be conditioned (condition is expressed as data item name), the condition enables or disables the entry. Beacuse the condition can be changed anyhow, it is easily possible to integrate the calendar to the control system.

text.p: SDAP (Simple Data Access Protocol) allows a remote access to the server data items and concurrently also allows to perform some administrative tasks. SDAP is a text line protocol transferred with help of TCP from the SmartServer on port 6007 (the port can be changed in configuration, see the chapter). After connection to the server, no control data are transferred by the protocol. After its establishing, the connection is permanent till its termination by the client. In case of unrecognised outage of the network, the server will complete the connection to 2 minutes, approximately.

SDAP confirms (response) all orders/requirements for server (request). If the confirmation will not come after sending of the command, the command was neither accepted, nor elaborated. All commands and responses are completed with signs CR and LF.

To maintain compatibility with older version, context of SDAP client is initialized to .KNX. That means all KNX data are accessible directly, without specifying context. Data outside of KNX is possible to operate using complete name (e.g. .System.Project) or using SDAP context command. To know more about context and data names see chapter.

Each line of the protocol contains well formed XML with data details. After its establishing, the connection is permanent till its termination by the client. In case of unrecognised outage of the network, the server will complete the connection to 2 minutes, approximately.
XMLSocket interface uses fixed .KNX. Different data items must be accessed using complete names only.
